building.name: Massachusetts State Building Code, 780 CMR, Tenth Edition, Base Volume (2021 International Building Code with Massachusetts amendments). Boston has no building code of its own: 780 CMR is the building code for every city and town.
building.effective: 2024-10-11 (Mass. Register Issue 1532). The state-codes file records a period in which the Ninth Edition could still be used, ending June 30, 2025; that date was not read on an official page.
building.quote: [101.1] The Board of Building Regulations and Standards ("BBRS") adopts and incorporates by reference, the International Building Code-2021 ("IBC"), as periodically amended by errata, the following chapters, as well as 110.R1 through 110.R7 and Appendices A through O. These, together with modifications as set forth, shall collectively comprise 780 CMR, otherwise known as the Massachusetts State Building Code, Tenth Edition, Base Volume. [...] Amended by Mass Register Issue 1532, eff. 10/11/2024. [101.2] 780 CMR shall be the building code for all towns, cities, state agencies or authorities in accordance with M.G.L. c. 143, §§ 93 through 100.
building.note: Read on Cornell LII's copy of 780 CMR (secondary): mass.gov returns HTTP 403 to automated access. No Boston page read names the edition; the city's permit guide says Inspectional Services 'administers and enforces building, housing, health, sanitation, and safety regulations mandated by City and State governments'.

plumbing.name: Uniform State Plumbing Code, 248 CMR 10.00 (written by the Massachusetts Board of State Examiners of Plumbers and Gas Fitters; not the International or Uniform Plumbing Code)
plumbing.edition: As amended effective December 8, 2023 (Mass. Register Issue 1510), per the state pack
plumbing.effective: 2023-12-08 (latest amendment on the copy the state pack read)
plumbing.quote: [M.G.L. c. 142, § 13] In all cities and towns, the examiners shall make and from time to time in like manner alter, amend and repeal rules and regulations relative to the construction, alteration, repair and inspection of plumbing in such cities and towns, which rules and regulations shall be reasonable, uniform and based on generally accepted standards of plumbing practice; provided, however, that the application of such rules and regulations may be varied by the examiners in a particular city or town upon petition of the board of health or health department thereof. [780 CMR 101.4.3] Reference to the International Plumbing Code or International Fuel Gas Code shall be considered reference to 248 CMR: Board of State Examiners of Plumbers and Gas Fitters.
plumbing.note: The statute lets the state board vary how the rules apply in one city on petition of its board of health. No such variance for Boston was found; the Board's own pages (mass.gov) could not be opened.

codes.scheduled_change_note: None found. The state pack notes that the plumbing board was redrafting 248 CMR 10.00 and the Architectural Access Board was drafting changes to 521 CMR during 2026, with no final amendment found.
codes.authority: City of Boston Inspectional Services Department (ISD), 1010 Massachusetts Avenue, 5th Floor, Boston, MA 02118; 617-635-5300; isd@boston.gov. Under 780 CMR 103.1 the code is enforced by the building official (the building commissioner or inspector of buildings, local inspector and state building inspector). Plumbing is inspected by the city's inspectors of plumbing (M.G.L. c. 142, § 11).
codes.authority_quote: [ISD, Navigating the Permit Process] Who is responsible for building permits? Inspectional Services administers and enforces building, housing, health, sanitation, and safety regulations mandated by City and State governments. Permits for construction projects include building, electrical, plumbing, and gas must be applied for before doing work. [780 CMR 103.1] 780 CMR shall be enforced by the building official, and in accordance with M.G.L. c. 143, §§ 3, 3A, 3Y, and 3Z and M.G.L. c. 22, the building official shall include the building commissioner or inspector of buildings, local inspector, and state building inspector.

fixtures.city_amends_note: Boston does not set toilet counts. The counts come from the state plumbing code (248 CMR 10.10, Table 1), which state law requires to be uniform in all cities and towns (M.G.L. c. 142, § 13); the building code hands plumbing to 248 CMR (780 CMR 101.4.3 and 2901.1 as amended). No Boston ordinance, bulletin or page changing the table, the urinal share, the 50/50 split or the 20-person exception was found on boston.gov. The Boston Municipal Code (American Legal Publishing) blocks automated access and was not read. The state pack's worked examples stand, counted by seats and staff, not floor area.
fixtures.worked_examples_note: Not redone: the state pack's twelve examples apply (office 2/1, 3/2, 5/4, 7/6; restaurant 1/1, 2/1, 4/2, 8/4; school 1/1, 2/2, 4/4, 6/6 at 50, 100, 200 and 400 people; women's/men's, urinals optional up to half of the men's toilets).

permit.exempt_list_quote: [780 CMR 105.1] It shall be unlawful to construct, reconstruct, alter, repair, remove or demolish a building or structure; or to change the use or occupancy of a building or structure; or to install or alter any equipment or life safety systems for which provision is made or the installation of which is regulated by 780 CMR without first filing an application with the building official and obtaining the required permit. [780 CMR 105.2 Work Exempt from Permit] While other kinds of permits may be required for work governed by other laws, by-laws, rules and the specialized codes of M.G.L. c. 143, § 96, such as electrical, plumbing, and sheet metal, a permit pursuant to 780 CMR is not required for the following activities: 1. One-story detached accessory structures used as tool and storage sheds, playhouses and similar uses, provided the floor area is not greater than 120 ft.2 (11 m2). 2. Fences not over seven feet (2,134 mm) high. 3. Oil derricks. 4. Retaining walls that are not over four feet (1,219 mm) in height [...] 5. Water tanks supported directly on grade [...] 6. Sidewalks and driveways not more than 30 inches (762 mm) above adjacent grade [...] 7. Painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work. 8. Temporary motion picture, television and theater stage sets and scenery. 9. Prefabricated swimming pools accessory to a Group R-3 occupancy [...] 10. Shade cloth structures constructed for nursery or agricultural purposes, not including service systems. 11. Swings and other playground equipment accessory to detached one- and two-family dwellings. 12. Window awnings in Group R-3 and U occupancies [...] 13. Non-fixed and movable fixtures, cases, racks, counters and partitions not over five feet nine inches (1,753 mm) in height. 14. Greenhouses covered exclusively with plastic film. [...] 15. Repair of any component or components of a fire protection system, where such does not affect system performance and compatibility. No permit pursuant to 780 CMR is required for routine or corrective maintenance. [105.2.2 Repairs] Application or notice to the building official is not required for ordinary repairs to structures. A permit is required for work including but not limited to: the substantial cutting away of any wall, partition or portion thereof, the removal or cutting of any structural beam or load bearing support, or the removal or change of any required means of egress, or rearrangement of parts of a structure affecting the egress requirements or mechanical systems or other work affecting public health or general safety under the jurisdiction of 780 CMR. [boston.gov, Short-Form Permit] A Short-Form Permit covers minor alterations that don't change a building's structure or use. [...] You may need a Short-Form Permit if you are opening up a wall, or working on minor alterations, repairs, or replacements that do not change the structure or use of a home, building, or lot. [...] Contact Inspectional Services if you're not sure which one you need. [...] Fees $20, plus $10 per $1,000 of estimated cost. [ISD, Navigating the Permit Process] Short-Form/Minor Permit: These are required for minor work and jobs that do not change a building's: a) Use or exits, b) Fire protection, c) Or living area.
permit.partitions_named_note: Toilet partitions are not named. The only partitions on the exempt list are 'non-fixed and movable' ones not over 5 feet 9 inches; toilet partitions are fixed to the floor, wall or ceiling. Whether a like-for-like replacement is 'similar finish work', an 'ordinary repair' or a minor replacement that needs Boston's Short-Form Permit is not stated on any page read. The exempt list is the state's (780 CMR 105.2, as amended by Massachusetts, read on Cornell LII); Boston publishes no list of its own.

public_wage.city_rule: Boston Jobs, Living Wage, and Prevailing Wage Ordinance: workers on City of Boston service contracts and subcontracts worth at least $25,000 must be paid the city's living wage, $19.36 an hour from July 1, 2026 (adjusted each July). Janitorial staff and security guards on city building service contracts and covered leases are paid from a state prevailing wage schedule, whatever the contract size. The page read describes service and building service contracts, not construction; construction on city projects falls under the state prevailing wage law. The ordinance text (American Legal Publishing) was not read.
public_wage.city_rule_quote: All workers employed on City of Boston service contracts and subcontracts worth at least $25,000 must be paid the living wage. This wage amount is adjusted each July. As of July 1, 2026, the living wage is $19.36.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Boston job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the Massachusetts rules Boston enforces.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Boston offices, hospitals, university buildings and restaurants, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Massachusetts sets the number of toilets by how many people a building is set up for, and the same state table applies in Boston. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** in Boston, as everywhere in Massachusetts, a permit is needed to alter or repair a building, and the state's building rules list the work that needs none. The list covers painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, countertops and similar finish work, movable partitions no taller than 5 feet 9 inches, and ordinary repairs. It doesn't name toilet partitions fixed to the floor or wall. Boston issues a Short-Form Permit for minor alterations, repairs and replacements that don't change a building's structure or use, so ask the Inspectional Services Department (617-635-5300) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.install_rule: In Boston the contractor applies for the permit and holds the Massachusetts construction supervisor license where the work requires it. Massachusetts has no general contractor license for commercial interior work, and its home improvement contractor registration covers only owner-occupied homes of one to four units. Work that needs a building permit may have to be supervised by a licensed construction supervisor, so check with Boston's Inspectional Services Department. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: In Boston the contractor applies for any permit the work needs.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on state, county, city, town and school district construction, Massachusetts law requires at least the wage rates the state Department of Labor Standards sets for that project, with no minimum project size in the law. The state issues the rates project by project. On a schedule it issued for a Boston school job in April 2026, a carpenter's rate from September 1, 2026 is $63.69 an hour plus $30.55 in benefits, rising to $65.19 an hour on March 1, 2027.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 6.25% in Boston. That is the Massachusetts state rate, set by state law for sales of goods across the state.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hospitals, universities and labs:** phenolic or stainless steel where restrooms are cleaned many times a day, HDPE in student buildings that see hard use.
sources: - Codes Boston enforces: Massachusetts State Building Code, 780 CMR, Tenth Edition, [section 101.1, Adoption and Title](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/massachusetts/780-CMR-101-101-1), [section 101.2, Scope](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/massachusetts/780-CMR-101-101-2) (the building code for all cities and towns), [section 101.4, Referenced Codes and Standards](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/massachusetts/780-CMR-101-101-4) (plumbing is 248 CMR) and [section 103.1, Municipal and State Enforcement](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/massachusetts/780-CMR-103-103-1), amended effective October 11, 2024, read on Cornell's Legal Information Institute copy; the official page is [mass.gov, Tenth Edition of the MA State Building Code 780](https://www.mass.gov/handbook/tenth-edition-of-the-ma-state-building-code-780). Plumbing rules are uniform in all cities and towns: [Massachusetts General Laws chapter 142, section 13](https://malegislature.gov/Laws/GeneralLaws/PartI/TitleXX/Chapter142/Section13). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Permits in Boston: 780 CMR [section 105.1, Required](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/massachusetts/780-CMR-105-105-1) and [section 105.2, Work Exempt from Permit](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/massachusetts/780-CMR-105-105-2), with 105.2.2, Repairs, read on Cornell's Legal Information Institute copy; City of Boston, [Short-Form Permit](https://www.boston.gov/permitting/permits/short-form-permit) and [Long-Form Permit](https://www.boston.gov/permitting/permits/long-form-permit); Inspectional Services Department, [Navigating the Permit Process](https://www.boston.gov/sites/default/files/file/2024/02/ISD_Navigating%20the%20Permit%20Process%20Eng.pdf) and [department page](https://www.boston.gov/departments/inspectional-services) (617-635-5300). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Wages on public jobs in Boston: Massachusetts Department of Labor Standards, Prevailing Wage Rates, Wage Request Number 20260429163828, issued April 30, 2026 for City/Town Boston (Carpenter, Carpenters Zone 1 (Metro Boston): $63.69 base wage, $10.58 health, $11.47 pension and $8.50 annuity from September 1, 2026; $65.19 base wage from March 1, 2027), as included in [Match Charter Public School's June 2026 bid documents](https://matchschool.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/June-2026_Elevator_small.pdf). Rates are set for each project under Massachusetts General Laws chapter 149, sections 26 and 27. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Sales tax rate and its start date: [Massachusetts General Laws chapter 64H, section 2](https://malegislature.gov/Laws/GeneralLaws/PartI/TitleIX/Chapter64H/Section2) (6.25%) and [Acts of 2009, chapter 27, sections 53 and 155](https://malegislature.gov/Laws/SessionLaws/Acts/2009/Chapter27) (in effect since August 1, 2009). Checked 2026-11-24.
